candidates.computation_change_reason: The segment header locates this text in part_i while the body labels it as Appendix A of Part II; resolving which permit part/appendix governs affects whether these MQL values are the operative reporting thresholds for compliance evaluation under A, the reporting obligations tied to monitoring under B, and the evidentiary rules for below-quantification or missing results under C.

candidates.exact_span: The following Minimum Quantification Levels (MQL’s) are to be used for reporting pollutant data for NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether MQLs apply only to permit applications, only to compliance reporting, or both determines if reported measurements must be evaluated against these quantification thresholds when comparing to discharge limits (A), whether compliance reporting itself is an applicable monitoring/reporting obligation (B), and how sub-MQL or non-quantified results are classified versus true missing evidence (C).

Two distinct MQL values are listed for Mercury with footnote *1 but no footnote text appears in this segment; choosing 0.0005 versus 0.005 changes whether mercury results are treated as quantified or below quantification, which in turn changes enforceable limit exceedance determinations (A) and the missing-/non-detect evidence classification (C).

The table specifies MQL units as µg/l; if applicable discharge limits or reported measurements are expressed in different units, interpretation of unit conversion and comparability affects whether a measurement can be compared to a limit (A) and whether a reported value is above or below the operative quantification level (C).

This row specifies a distinct MQL for weak-acid-dissociable cyanide rather than total cyanide (listed separately at 10 µg/l); applying the wrong cyanide form's MQL would change quantification status of reported cyanide measurements and thus limit-exceedance and missing-evidence outcomes for cyanide parameters.

Residual chlorine is listed separately from the cyanide/chlorine group header; misinterpreting which chlorine species this MQL covers could change whether reported chlorine measurements are treated as quantified for compliance comparison (A) or classified as below-quantification/no-data (C).
